records.quote: For sooty flames, results show that the absence of gravity can have a major effect. Flames are taller, wider, cooler, and far sootier in microgravity as compared to normal gravity.
records.derivation: Under 'SELECTED FINDINGS' in the CLD Flame section of a NASA Glenn fact sheet (outside PSI). It reports this experiment's results for sooty flames burned in microgravity; R2 covers the diluted flames. The same page says the experiment covers both ends: 'pure-fuel flames that produce soot, and highly diluted flames that are close to extinction'. The fact sheet does not list test days.

records.quote: The data has shown that for highly diluted weak flames, microgravity flames are more stable than their normal gravity counterparts.
records.derivation: Same 'SELECTED FINDINGS' list as R1, for the diluted flames. The fact sheet does not list test days.

records.quote: The enhanced time and spatial scales in a microgravity environment will be important for achieving both goals.
records.derivation: A plan ('will be important'), not a statement that the tests were run in microgravity. section=researchImpacts has another goal sentence of the same kind: 'A goal of the study will be to apply sophisticated numerical tools and quantitative diagnostic techniques to the study of hydrocarbon diffusion flames in a microgravity environment.'
PSI category label for the whole investigation, not a sentence about the test conditions.

records.quote: Soot volume fraction measurements indicate that microgravity flames contain five to eight times more soot than the equivalent normal gravity flames.
records.derivation: The fact sheet reports measured normal-gravity flames used for comparison, but does not say where or when they were burned, or whether they belong to this investigation. No PSI table row is labelled as a normal-gravity test (Test Type values: 'Methane based test', 'Ethylene based test', 'Improved coflow tests'). This record matches no table row.
PSI record label for the whole investigation. The fuels named in section=objective are methane and ethylene.
The ACME chamber insert in the CIR is shared by the six ACME experiments listed in the fact sheet (BRE, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame, CFI-G). See lineage.

records.quote: Measurements will be made of the structure of diluted methane and ethylene flames in an air coflow.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. Stream: the oxidizer coflow around the fuel jet; the sentence does not say what gas filled the chamber. The sentence is written as a plan ('will be made'). The nitrogen that dilutes the fuel (fact sheet p.3: 'nitrogen in our case'; CSV row=1 Notes) is the fuel stream, not this one.

records.quote: Characterize the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, lift-off heights, temperatures and extinction limits.
records.derivation: Objective A of the PSI record. The investigation title (section=title) also names the configuration: 'Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame'.

records.quote: Measurements will be made of the structure of diluted methane and ethylene flames in an air coflow.
records.derivation: The sentence is written as a plan ('will be made').

not_found.looked_in: PSI record text (all sections); CSV Notes column (row=1 is the only note); fact sheet CLD Flame section pp.2-4. The fact sheet says 'air coflow' (p.3) but gives no oxygen number, so no value is proposed.

PSI record text (all sections); CSV Notes column row=1; fact sheet CLD Flame section pp.2-4. The only pressure sentence is ACME-wide, not CLD-specific, and has no value (p.18: 'All ACME experiments will be constant volume (i.e., rather than constant pressure) studies, where the chamber’s free volume will be about 90 liters.').

PSI record section=objective ('as a function of velocity', no value); fact sheet pp.2-3 ('injection velocity', no value); CSV Notes row=1 gives only the full-scale range of the mass flow controllers ('in slpm on a nitrogen basis'), which is a flow-rate capacity, not a coflow velocity. The Test Type column labels data rows 29-32 (test days 21041, 21046, 21050, 21062) 'Improved coflow tests' but states no velocity.

lineage: CLD Flame ran on the ACME hardware in the CIR on the ISS (record section=experimentHardware: 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'; CSV row=1 Notes: 'MFC - identifies the maximum flow rate of the specified ACME Mass Flow Controller (MFC) in slpm on a nitrogen basis.'). The fact sheet, ACME-wide, p.9: 'The ACME experiments will be conducted with a single modular set of hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS), where the CIR is depicted below.' The fact sheet describes six ACME experiments (BRE, CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame, CFI-G); p.1 says 'five' in one sentence and 'six' in another. E-FIELD Flames planned to use the CLD burner configuration (p.5: 'The experiment will be conducted with a normal coflow flame (as in the CLD Flame experiment) or perhaps with a simple gas-jet flame, where there is no surrounding coflow.'). E-FIELD Flames uses an electric field; it is not a gravity data point. SLICE (MSG, 2012) is called an ACME precursor (p.1), not shared hardware.
